title: Special City Council Meeting
overview: At a short special meeting, the Glendale City Council accepted $1 million in state money and approved using it for tech startup programs. The council voted 4–0 to let the City Manager sign deals giving $500,000 each over three years to FoundersBoost and SmartGateVC. Councilmember Najarian did not answer the roll call.

items.title: Community Development, re: Acceptance of state funds from the State of California Governor's Office of Business and Economic Development; and Authorization to Negotiate with Up to Two Tech Startup Growth Program Proposer(s) to Develop and Implement the Startup Growth Program(s)
items.headline: Council accepts $1 million state grant and splits it between two tech startup programs
items.summary: The state's business office (GO-Biz) gave Glendale $1 million. State Senator Anthony Portantino helped get the money. Staff picked two groups from 17 proposals to run startup programs for three years, with $500,000 each. FoundersBoost will work with Hacker Fund and the Alliance for SoCal Innovation on the Glendale Growth Alliance, which plans startup training programs, called accelerators, and quarterly hackathons. SmartGateVC will run a Venture Building Program that helps turn university research, especially in artificial intelligence, into new companies. Many callers spoke in support, and the council approved accepting the money, budgeting it (an "appropriation"), and letting the City Manager sign the contracts.
items.whyItMatters: Glendale will fund new programs to help local startups, students and entrepreneurs, which the city hopes will bring more tech jobs and investment.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: Thank you, Mr. Galanian. Good afternoon, Madam Mayor and City Council members. We are so excited to be here today to present an opportunity that we believe will further support and strengthen Glendale's tech and innovation ecosystem.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: But before we dive in, I would like to also take an opportunity to recognize and extend our gratitude to the Governor's Office of Business and Economic Development and State Senator Anthony Portantino. Back in 2019, he saw the potential of Glendale's growing tech community and secured 1 million in funding to help support startups and also build innovation here in the city.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: This year, Senator Portantino once again championed an additional round of funding to ensure that we can sustain and also grow and accelerate the startup ecosystem here in Glendale. So we are incredibly grateful for his continued support and also commitment to Glendale's tech community.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: In the next few slides, we will walk you through the key milestones and achievements that have helped shaped our tech and innovation journey up to this point. We'll also cover why startup ecosystems matter, dive into the RFP process, and then conclude with staff recommendations.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: So let's begin with the core foundation of this journey. In February 2016, the city partnered with Estolano Advisors to develop a roadmap for growing Glendale's technology sector. This resulted in the formation of the Glendale Tech Strategy, which was published and adopted by City Council in 2017.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: This strategy has been our guiding framework, if you will, c- driving our continuous efforts to support and nurture the tech community in Glendale.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: Since the adoption of the tech strategy, economic development has successfully implemented several recommendations, including continuation of Glendale Tech on Tap, which are monthly meetups uniting the tech community in a casual setting to discuss ideas and trends, and also to connect with other entrepreneurs.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: In collaboration with multiple partners, we hosted our ninth annual Glendale Tech Week last month, which attracted nearly 3,000 founders, investors, and community members across 22 events throughout the week, which is a testament to its growing impact and success.

transcript.speaker: speaker_0
transcript.text: Oh.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: And thanks to the 1 million in state funding secured in 2019, we introduced two startup accelerators, Hero House and Kids X, with contracts in place with these partners from 2021 to 2023.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: So o- over the past couple of years, we have expanded our resources and initiatives so that we can better support local businesses and startups. That includes we produced a How to Do Business in Glendale guide to offer insights to businesses and business owners as well who are looking at establishing a location here in our city.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: We also implemented the annual Let's Grow Glendale Small Business Summit, and this past May we hosted the second annual event, attracting nearly 400 attendees, double the turnout of the inaugural year. The summit brought together businesses, government leaders, and nonprofits to provide valuable business information and resources, including networking opportunities, 'cause again, we want to ensure that our small businesses grow and thrive here in the city.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: We also launched a free human resource hotline, which is important especially for Glendale employers to offer expert guidance on labor and wage laws, hiring practices, labor regulations, and much more.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: So in June of 2022, City Council approved the city's very first three-year economic development strategic plan, reaffirming our commitment to strengthening the tech ecosystem here and to drive sustainable economic growth in the city. The plan identifies four key pillars, as you can see on the screen, starting with enhancing Glendale's brand identity so that we can position the city as a top choice to live, to work, to experience, and to invest.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: The second element is fostering a business-friendly culture that supports business attraction as well as retention purposes.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: Followed by growing the tech and innovation industry so that we can attract and retain talent while also supporting the growth and success of entrepreneurs. And lastly, expanding our arts and entertainment offerings to provide a healthy mix of amenities for our residents, as well as to promote Glendale as a top destination for visitors.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: So as you can see, growing the tech and innovation ecosystem is at the heart of this plan, and by aligning our strategic efforts with the growth of our sector, we are ensuring that Glendale remains a competitive and business-friendly city that embraces innovation for the benefit of the entire community.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: And now I would like to turn it over to David Crowley-Delgado, our senior economic development coordinator, for the next portion of the presentation. David actually joined the city in January of this year and brings extensive experience as a former innovation strategist at the CHLA Innovation Studio.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: Since he started, he has been extremely instrumental in really driving our tech initiatives here, and he also served as the project manager during the tech RFP process.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: Welcome, David.

transcript.speaker: speaker_6
transcript.text: Thank you, Shuah. Thank you very much. Um, Madam Mayor and Council, it's a privilege to work as part of this team as we build an even brighter future for this Jewel City. As part of this presentation, we wanted to make sure we're explaining the broader context of this work and why it remains relevant. Since the adoption of the tech strategy, the city has placed an emphasis on building and maintaining a vibrant startup ecosystem to drive innovation, economic growth, and job creation.

transcript.speaker: speaker_6
transcript.text: According to the Harvard Business Review, vibrant startup ecosystems attract talent and investment and create a multiplying effect where new businesses stimulate demand for services and infrastructure. Additionally, the Kauffman Foundation highlights that startups are a primary source of net new job creation, often outpacing larger firms in growth. Cities with strong ecosystems foster collaboration between academia, government, and the private sector, spurring technological advancements, positioning the city as a hub for entrepreneurial activity, and enhancing the city's global competitiveness and resilience.

transcript.speaker: speaker_6
transcript.text: So how's the health of our ecosystem here in Glendale? We have a very strong tech presence here within the city, with three unicorns on Brand Boulevard, media and innovation giants such as The Walt Disney Company, and hundreds of small and medium-sized tech startups, and this number is growing. In total, high-tech companies employ over twelve thousand individuals within the city.

transcript.speaker: speaker_6
transcript.text: The city also boasts a robust network of support services and proactive government that is proudly business-friendly in approach and policy. While we have a strong tech industry presence, our tech ecosystem has an opportunity to be strengthened. We have a small yet growing investment community and are home to f- a few hyper-targeted accelerator programs, such as Hero House and the Disney Accelerator, who provide a large impact on a fairly narrow group of companies.

transcript.speaker: speaker_6
transcript.text: While foundationally strong, this growing ecosystem has the need for additional programs to fill some of the remaining gaps. There still exists an opportunity to expand the number of services available to startups and create stronger connections to corporate partners, educational institutions, and the entrepreneurs driving innovation here in Glendale. The purpose of this RFP is to recruit, select, and fund programs that will showcase the local startup community and provide emerging companies with the tools and support they need to thrive in today's market, to promote Glendale and the region as an innovation hub, to attract and retain a diverse pool of tech talent in Glendale and the broader area, and to drive local economic development through supporting entrepreneurs and potential high-growth startups that may generate revenue, create high-paying jobs,

transcript.speaker: speaker_6
transcript.text: and create products and ideas that are solving meaningful problems. In order to achieve the city's goal of diversifying and broadening the startup ecosystem within the city, the RFP was written to split the one million dollar grant between two operators over the course of the three-year term. Submissions included an overview of the proposed growth programs as well as a budget for how the five hundred thousand dollars in funds would be utilized.

transcript.speaker: speaker_6
transcript.text: Applicants had the option to include in their proposal a second program structure and budget for the full one million dollars if the selection committee could consider that as well.

transcript.speaker: speaker_6
transcript.text: The RFP was distributed widely in order to attract the highest tier of applicant. In addition to the typical outlets that the city uses, the RFP was distributed to the local and national outlets specific to the tech community. All applicants of the 2019 grant were also invited to apply. In total, the RFP was distributed to one hundred and ninety-four publications and journalists, community groups, and interested parties, many of whom redistributed the information on their own platforms.

transcript.speaker: speaker_6
transcript.text: This allowed visibility that attracted applicants from across the entire United States. The selection committee was comprised of subject matter experts with diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and expertise. We selected judges to fit seven personas representing viewpoints that allowed for a recommendation that has considered how the operators will improve the city's tech ecosystem, advance the startups within their programs, increase the city's reputation, and elevate the city's role as a collaborative and driving member of the SoCal tech scene.

transcript.speaker: speaker_6
transcript.text: In total, 17 proposals met the requirements for this RFP and were reviewed by the selection committee. The top five proposals were brought in for interviews. The committee identified two proposals that, in their expert opinion, best achieved the RFP's goals and advanced the t- city's tech strategy. The two proposals are the Glendale Growth Alliance led by FoundersBoost, and Venture Building Program led by SmartGateVC.

transcript.speaker: speaker_6
transcript.text: The FoundersBoost Foundation proposes partnering with The Hacker Fund and the Alliance for SoCal Innovation to establish, launch, and operate the Glendale Growth Alliance. This program aims to support underrepresented founders from the LA region, attracting them to the Glendale ecosystem. The core initiative revolves around biannual FoundersBoost accelerators focused on scalable tech startups led by underrepresented founders.

transcript.speaker: speaker_6
transcript.text: Graduates will receive support to enter the Alliance for SoCal Innovation's SoCal Venture Pipeline, providing them with further opportunities for growth and investment. In addition, the Glendale Growth Alliance has proposed hosting large scale hackathons within the City of Glendale hosted by The Hacker Fund, bringing together students, entrepreneurs, and innovators from across the region to collectively solve pressing problems.

transcript.speaker: speaker_6
transcript.text: The selection committee appreciated how these programs touched on every stage of the startup journey, from idea development through company founding and growth. Additionally, the committee appreciated the focus on providing opportunity for underrepresented founders, as well as engaging students and the non-founder community.

transcript.speaker: speaker_6
transcript.text: SmartGateVC proposes a Venture Building Program, which will be a premier studio located here within the City of Glendale. Its mission will be to bridge the gap between cutting-edge research and market-ready products by fostering collaborations between academic institutions and industry leaders. With a focus on labora- laboratories and universities across Southern California, the proposed Venture Building Program will be dedicated to building companies from groundbreaking technologies, focusing on real-world applications of artificial intelligence.

transcript.speaker: speaker_6
transcript.text: The objective will be to build businesses, to help founders raise pre-seed funding following the program, to establish operations here in Glendale, and to acquire their very first paying customers. The selection committee saw value in the, this bridge that would be created between the research insti- institutions and the business community, and recognizes how this program will greatly strengthen the incubator network within Glendale and the broader LA region.

transcript.speaker: speaker_6
transcript.text: Funding both programs will allow these two operators to work symbiotically, not detracting from either program, but allowing each to amplify the other's impact. The selection committee feels confident that funding these two programs will be a powerful step for the city towards achieving the vision of Glendale as a vibrant tech hub.

transcript.speaker: speaker_6
transcript.text: Additionally, I'd like to quickly walk through the key milestones in this process. The RFP was released on May 15th of 2024, and after a pre-bid conference and a period to submit written questions and receive answers, proposals were due on July 12th. After reviewing all the proposals, the selection committee identified the top five and invited those operators to follow-up interviews during the week of August 20th.

transcript.speaker: speaker_6
transcript.text: After discussion and deliberation, the committee reached a unanimous vote to recommend awarding $500,000 each over three years to the Venture Building Program and the Glendale Glo- Growth Alliance program.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: Thank you, David. So to quickly recap, both applicants have a proven track record of building successful startup ecosystems locally. They are dedicated to supporting Glendale's technology growth and remain actively engaged in fostering collaboration and innovation within the community. In addition, they both have strong connections to Glendale and the broader tech community, including ties with educational institutions, investors, startups, uh, you name it.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: They also have expressed a strong commitment to remaining in Glendale, further solidifying their role in our community's growth. And these efforts align perfectly with the goals and objectives of our economic development strategic plan and the Glendale tech strategy. So we are definitely feeling confident in terms of their continued partnership as far as it driving local innovation and also elevating Glendale's global brand and reputation as a tech hub.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: So in closing, I would like to express our sincere gratitude to City Council for your leadership and ongoing support of economic development. A very special thank you to the amazing selection committee for all of their time and hard work throughout this intensive process. I also wanna take a moment to thank all the interested applicants for dedicating a lot of time and effort in putting together their proposals and submitting it to the city.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: And lastly, I also want to acknowledge our very own Sevak Dashoyan in ac- in economic development for his creativity and assistance in putting together this PowerPoint presentation. So this leads me to the staff recommendation. We recommend that City Council accept the $1 million in state funding and allocate the funds for the Tech Startup Growth Programs, followed by authorize the city manager or designee to negotiate and execute all agreements and related documents with both FoundersBoost and SmartGateVC in the amount of $500,000 each for a period of three years.

transcript.speaker: speaker_5
transcript.text: So with that, this concludes our presentation. We're happy to answer any questions you may have. We also have both operators in the audience to answer questions as well. Thank you.

hy.overview: Կարճ արտահերթ նիստի ժամանակ Գլենդելի քաղաքային խորհուրդը ընդունեց նահանգից $1 միլիոն գումար և հաստատեց այն օգտագործել տեխնոլոգիական սթարթափների ծրագրերի համար։ Խորհուրդը 4–0 քվեարկությամբ թույլատրեց Քաղաքի կառավարչին ստորագրել պայմանագրեր, որոնցով երեք տարվա ընթացքում $500,000-ական գումար կտրամադրվի FoundersBoost-ին և SmartGateVC-ին։ Խորհրդի անդամ Նաջարյանը չպատասխանեց անվանական ստուգմանը։

item-1.headline: Խորհուրդն ընդունում է նահանգի $1 միլիոն դրամաշնորհը և այն բաժանում երկու տեխնոլոգիական սթարթափ ծրագրերի միջև
item-1.summary: Նահանգի բիզնեսի գրասենյակը (GO-Biz) Գլենդելին տրամադրեց $1 միլիոն։ Նահանգային սենատոր Էնթընի Պորտանտինոն օգնեց ստանալ այդ գումարը։ Աշխատակազմը 17 առաջարկներից ընտրեց երկու կազմակերպություն, որոնք երեք տարի կղեկավարեն սթարթափ ծրագրեր՝ յուրաքանչյուրը ստանալով $500,000։ FoundersBoost-ը Hacker Fund-ի և Alliance for SoCal Innovation-ի հետ կաշխատի Glendale Growth Alliance-ի վրա, որը նախատեսում է սթարթափների ուսուցման ծրագրեր, այսպես կոչված «արագացուցիչներ» (accelerators), և եռամսյակային հաքաթոններ։ SmartGateVC-ն կղեկավարի Venture Building Program-ը, որն օգնում է համալսարանական հետազոտությունները, հատկապես արհեստական բանականության ոլորտում, վերածել նոր ընկերությունների։ Շատ զանգահարողներ արտահայտվեցին ի պաշտպանություն, և խորհուրդը հաստատեց գումարի ընդունումը, այն բյուջեում հատկացնելը («appropriation») և Քաղաքի կառավարչին պայմանագրերը ստորագրելու թույլտվություն տալը։
item-1.whyItMatters: Գլենդելը կֆինանսավորի նոր ծրագրեր՝ տեղական սթարթափներին, ուսանողներին և ձեռնարկատերերին օգնելու համար, ինչը, քաղաքի հույսով, կբերի ավելի շատ տեխնոլոգիական աշխատատեղեր և ներդրումներ։

es.overview: En una breve reunión especial, el Concejo Municipal de Glendale aceptó $1 millón en fondos estatales y aprobó usarlos para programas de empresas emergentes de tecnología (startups). El concejo votó 4–0 para permitir que el Administrador Municipal firme acuerdos que otorgan $500,000 a cada uno, durante tres años, a FoundersBoost y SmartGateVC. El concejal Najarian no respondió al pase de lista.

item-1.headline: El concejo acepta una subvención estatal de $1 millón y la divide entre dos programas de empresas emergentes de tecnología
item-1.summary: La oficina de negocios del estado (GO-Biz) le dio a Glendale $1 millón. El senador estatal Anthony Portantino ayudó a conseguir el dinero. El personal municipal eligió a dos grupos, entre 17 propuestas, para dirigir programas para empresas emergentes durante tres años, con $500,000 cada uno. FoundersBoost trabajará con Hacker Fund y la Alliance for SoCal Innovation en la Glendale Growth Alliance, que planea programas de capacitación para empresas emergentes, llamados aceleradoras, y hackatones cada tres meses. SmartGateVC dirigirá un Venture Building Program que ayuda a convertir investigaciones universitarias, especialmente en inteligencia artificial, en nuevas empresas. Muchas personas llamaron para expresar su apoyo, y el concejo aprobó aceptar el dinero, incluirlo en el presupuesto (una "asignación") y permitir que el Administrador Municipal firme los contratos.
item-1.whyItMatters: Glendale financiará nuevos programas para ayudar a empresas emergentes, estudiantes y emprendedores locales, lo que la ciudad espera que traiga más empleos e inversión en tecnología.
